home.manifestoCol1: A network of companies, shared workspaces, an education that doesn't end in the classroom: they are not elements alongside the course of study — they are an integral part of it. Studying and entering the industry happen in the same place.
home.manifestoCol2: Students work side by side with people already in the industry — in the same network of companies, in the same spaces. storiaItems.title: Foundation
storiaItems.text: In 1999 Massimiliano Magagni and Susanna Goldoni founded Italy's first school to bring the US teaching approach to popular music to Bologna, in partnership with the Los Angeles Music Academy — now the Los Angeles College of Music. The Bachelor's degree is awarded in partnership with Coventry University: an international qualification, not a local certificate.

storiaItems.title: Offering
storiaItems.text: Over twenty-five years the course offering has grown from instrumental performance to composition for film and video games, through to film production and sound engineering.

storiaItems.title: The new name
storiaItems.text: In 2021 Music Academy became Creative Hub Academy: Creative Hub Bologna was also born, the incubator that is today the Innovation area.

storiaItems.title: Awards
storiaItems.text: The "L'Europa è QUI" award in 2020, ISO 9001:EA37 certification.

storiaItems.title: Research
storiaItems.text: With the University of Bologna's DAMS, Tecnopolo CNR and Clust-ER Create, the Academy experiments with technologies applied to music and audiovisual production and distribution.

storiaItems.title: The campus
storiaItems.text: Three recording, mastering and post-production studios, isobox, a live room, four production boxes, a main hall with virtual theatre, a VR/AR room, a radio studio. Around two million euros of investment, co-funded by the Emilia-Romagna Region.

teachersIntro: Creative Hub Academy's teachers are working professionals in the music industry, not teachers describing a job they no longer do. What you bring into the classroom, they're doing right now, outside these walls: on tour, in the studio, on stage.
Among them Angela Madonia, a vocal coach familiar to Amici audiences, and Stefania Martin, who has worked alongside Renato Zero and Mina.
academy.inMemoriaText: Bologna also counted Celso Valli among its teachers, the arranger and producer behind the sound of Vasco Rossi, Laura Pausini, Mina and Eros Ramazzotti. He passed away in 2025. What he taught here still shapes the way the Academy works today.

faq.title: What's the difference between university programmes and custom lessons?
faq.text: University programmes last three years (two for Masters) and award an international academic degree — Bachelor of Arts, Bachelor of Science or Master of Music. Custom lessons are flexible packages with no exams or final degree: for those who want to learn an instrument without committing to a multi-year programme.

faq.title: How does Region-funded training work?
faq.text: These are free courses funded by the European Social Fund Plus and the Emilia-Romagna Region, lasting a few months, with an internship included and a specialisation certificate recognised at regional level. They are not equivalent to a university degree.

faq.title: Can I visit an open day before choosing a course?
faq.text: Yes, that's exactly what it's for. You can visit the studios, meet the teachers and get a concrete idea before applying — even if you haven't decided which course is right for you.

faq.title: Can I study part-time if I already work?
faq.text: Yes, every university programme has a part-time option: same programme, spread over more time.

faq.title: The most common questions.

items.q: What's the difference between a Bachelor and an Italian degree?
items.a: The Bachelor of Arts or Bachelor of Science is a foreign first-cycle academic degree, EQF level 6. Outside Italy it is immediately spendable. For Italy, we support you in obtaining the Dichiarazione di Valore.
A motivational interview, not an exam. You need a high-school diploma, or an equivalent foreign qualification. Twenty places a year per programme.
Yes. Part-time means 60 credits a year instead of 120: the same programme, spread over more time. You can switch between modes during the course.

items.q: Do I need to already play, sing or shoot video?
items.a: No. Each programme starts from the basics of its field. What you need is motivation: technique is built over the three years.

items.q: How much does it cost, and can I pay in instalments?
items.a: Each programme has a zero-interest instalment plan. Details vary by programme and mode (full-time or part-time): you'll find them on each programme's page.

facts.s: follow the session in audio and video

registrazione.modesLede: We choose the method together, based on genre, budget and how you want the record to sound.

modes.title: All together
modes.text: The band plays in the same session, each instrument on its own track. The energy of a live take, with the option to fix things in the mix.

modes.title: One at a time
modes.text: Overdubs instrument by instrument: drums, bass, guitars, keys, vocals. For productions built layer by layer.

modes.title: From a distance
modes.text: You send us the project, we pick the right musicians for the genre and record for you. You follow live, wherever you are.

registrazione.liveText: Live room, control room and outer spaces are connected: musicians are isolated but see and hear each other in headphones, like on stage.
livePoints: Full bands: bass, drums, guitars, vocals and keys in the same session.
Strings and small orchestras: besides the live room you can use the natural reverb of the outer hall.
Every instrument stays on its own track, so the mix stays flexible.
what: Vocals, in an isolated booth with a Neumann U87
Guitars and bass, amplified or DI
Drums, in the 60 m² live room
String quartets, orchestral sections and small orchestras

remoteSteps.title: We record

faq.title: Can I record a full band together?

faq.title: Do I need an engineer?
faq.text: The studio engineer is included in the session. If you have your own, there's the full studio rental.

faq.title: What should I bring?
faq.text: Your instruments, your lyrics and your references. Drums, amps and backline are available in the studio.

finanziata.lede: Professional training for the cultural and creative industries: sound, music, data and 3D. Industry teachers, a few weeks or a few months, zero cost for you.

band.text: There are no open enrolments today. Music Data Analyst & Strategist is running: leave your contact details for the next edition.

finanziata.howLede: The courses are paid for by the Emilia-Romagna Region and the European Social Fund. That is why they have limited places, precise requirements and a selection. Here is how they work.

howItems.title: Who can take part
howItems.text: Anyone resident or domiciled in Emilia-Romagna, with a diploma or a vocational qualification. Each course has its own specific requirements.

howItems.title: How you get in
howItems.text: A written test, an individual interview and preferential criteria. The ranking is published on the site.

howItems.title: What you get
howItems.text: A certificate of attendance or a higher technical specialisation certificate (IFTS), depending on the course.

howItems.title: When
howItems.text: Enrolment stays open for a few weeks, when the call is published. To avoid missing it, leave your contact details.

finanziata.uniLede: The funded courses are short and vocational. If you want a three-year path with an international degree, have a look at the university courses: Bachelor and Master in music, sound and visual.
finanziata.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about the free courses.

faq.title: Are they really free?
faq.text: Yes. The courses are paid for by the Emilia-Romagna Region and the European Social Fund Plus: for those taking part the cost is zero.

faq.title: Do I have to live in Emilia-Romagna?
faq.text: You need residence or domicile in Emilia-Romagna. Each course then has its own specific requirements, written in the call.

faq.title: What qualification do I need?
faq.text: A secondary school diploma or a vocational qualification. The exact requirements change from course to course and are stated in the call.

faq.title: How does the selection work?
faq.text: A written test, an individual interview and preferential criteria. The ranking is published on the site.

faq.title: Can I take part if I work?
faq.text: Timetable, calendar and required attendance change from course to course and are stated in the call. Leave us your contact details: we will write as soon as it is out, so you can plan ahead.

faq.title: When does the next course open?
faq.text: There are no open enrolments today: Music Data Analyst & Strategist is running. Enrolment stays open for a few weeks, when the call is published: to avoid missing it, leave your contact details.
